provenance.orgName: Chester, Cheshire, Benedictine abbey of St Werburg
provenance.p: This attribution was accepted with a query in the second edition of Medieval Libraries of Great Britain (1964, p. 49). For comparison, the following note appeared under Chester St Werburg in the Supplement (1987, p. 14): Mostyn Hall MS. Post-Dissolution, therefore omit. This was almost certainly a mistake (specifically, an inadvertent duplication of the revised entry for this manuscript under Llantarnam; see later provenance below). Compare especially the description of the manuscript in The Mostyn Hall Library Printed Books and manuscripts Part III (Christie's, 23-24 October 1974, lot 1487). In this catalogue entry, the manuscript is dated to the fifteenth and early sixteenth centuries. The contents, which are described there in some detail, are said to leave no doubt that it was written in the Benedictine Abbey of St Werburgh.

history.provenance: Later (i.e. beyond the chronological scope of Medieval Libraries of Great Britain) at the Cistercian abbey of Llantarnam (Caerlion, Kairlion). According to the corresponding Medieval Libraries of Great Britain index card, there is an inscription, llyver e monach a Caerlleon on the vellum cover. This inscription was deemed sufficient to qualify the manuscript for entry (albeit with a query) under Llantarnam in the second edition of Medieval Libraries of Great Britain (1964, p. 23). However, the Llantarnam attribution was omitted in the Supplement on chronological grounds (1987, p. 7): Post-Dissolution, therefore omit. Compare the chronological limit of the project as described in the revised preface to the second edition (1964, p. viii): The limit of date is about 1540 for English and Welsh libraries.
Mostyn Hall, Lord Mostyn. This was the location reported in all of the published Medieval Libraries of Great Britain handlists.
Not in the Mostyn sale at Sotheby's, 13 July 1920.
Christie's, 23-24 October 1974, lot 1487 (The Mostyn Hall Library Printed Books and manuscripts Part III).
